rules.title: Rules
rules.sub: The anti-slop rules. ORC ships 65 of them, read-only. Yours win.
rules.unavailableHint: `orc rules --json` returned nothing this panel could parse. Run it in a terminal to see what it said.
rules.precedence.title: Precedence
rules.precedence.lead: Three layers, and the order never changes.
rules.precedence.houseScope: The house rules are CODE and behaviour only. They govern how a change is made — surgical, simple, honest. They say nothing about the words an agent writes, so they never overrule a writing rule.
rules.overrides.head: 1 ORC rule your rules replaced
rules.overrides.unknownId: not a known ORC rule id
rules.user.title: Your rules
rules.user.wins: This project's own standing instructions. They are read BEFORE ORC's rules, and they win wherever the two disagree.
rules.user.howto: Three headings — P0, P1, P2 — and as much text under each as you want. The whole block is handed to every agent verbatim, so write it the way you would say it. Anything above the first heading is a note to yourself and is never dispatched.
rules.user.turnOff: To switch an ORC rule off, name its id in a rule of your own: "OSW-13: em dashes are our house voice." The override is then counted, printed at preflight, and stated inside every slice.
rules.packs.title: ORC rules
rules.packs.lead: {n} rules in four packs, shipped with ORC. Adapted, with credit, from other people's work — see below.
rules.packs.filter: Filter by id, title or text
rules.packs.changeHow: These change with `orc update` and with nothing else. To change what ORC writes in this project, write your own rule above.
rules.packs.englishOnly: The rule text stays English in every language. It is shipped content that rule ids point at, and a translated rule would be a different rule.
rules.credits.title: Credits
rules.credits.lead: These rules are other people's work. Each source is named with its licence and what ORC took from it.
rules.lint.title: Lint
rules.lint.lead: A free check, zero tokens. It reads only what a string match can prove, and it always says how many rules it could not check. It reports; it never fixes.
rules.lint.pathPlaceholder: A file or folder, relative to the project
rules.lint.clean: Clean, on the rules a matcher can prove.
rules.lint.suppressed: Off here, because your own rules name these ids: {ids}
